ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: ailments and illnesses
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Rimfolk's everyday ailments and rare serious illnesses: where they come from, what they do and what helps
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Tend wounds within a few hours, keep a hat on in the heat, and keep fruit or vegetables on the table.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
Besides the game's own diseases, Rimfolk adds everyday ailments: small, temporary troubles from ordinary life. Some go round like a cold, through the game's own disease events; others come from how a colonist's day went, like a strained back after a day of hauling. None of them can kill or leaves a mark, and each says in its description what helps. Doctors tend them like any illness, and a colonist has at most two of the day-to-day kind at once.
A rare serious tier sits on top, behind its own setting: twelve illnesses modeled on real ones and two from the rim. Most of them can kill; measles, kidney stones and shingles can't, but they are hard going. At most one kind runs in the colony at a time, never within 30 days of the last, and each comes with a letter that says what it is and what helps. Steady tending beats all of them (for rabies, only if it starts before the symptoms show), appendicitis can also be cut out, and against the ones that real medicine treats with modern drugs, industrial or glitterworld medicine makes a much bigger difference than herbs.

li.heading: Going round

table.li: Ailment | Based on | When | Lasts | What helps
Head cold | The common cold | Any time, more in fall and winter | About a week | Bed rest, warmth; may leave a cough
Stomach bug | A stomach virus (norovirus) | Any time | 2 to 3 days | Rest and fluids; clean hands in the kitchen
Chest cold | Acute bronchitis | Below 5 °C outside | 9 to 12 days | Warmth (it worsens in the cold), rest; may leave a cough
Hay fever | A pollen allergy | Spring and summer, where plants grow | 4 to 9 days, longer outdoors | Indoor work; medicine, industrial best; comes back to the same people
Pinkeye | Conjunctivitis | Any time | About a week, 3 to 4 days with tending | Clean hands and towels; industrial medicine clears it fastest
Dreamfever | Invented | Any time | About a week | Rest and quiet; it brings vivid dreams

li.after: At 100%, one of these goes round about every 20 days on an average map, more often where the game's own diseases are common and less on gentler storyteller settings, and the same one at most once in 20 to 40 days. They hit a share of the colony the way the game's diseases do, never babies, and immunity, genes and the medical tab work as usual.

li.heading: From the day's work

table.li: Ailment | Comes from | Lasts | What helps
Strained back | 6 hours of hauling, mining or building in a day (never children) | 1 to 2 weeks | Bed rest at first, tending
Sore hands | 7 hours at a crafting, smithing, tailoring or art bench | About a week | Other work, tending
Blisters | 8 hours on the move with a caravan, on a map away from home or out hunting | 2 to 3 days | Tending, rest
Chilblains | 5 hours of outdoor work between -10 and 6 °C | About a week | Warmth, warm clothes
Sunburn | 4 hours outdoors around midday above 30 °C or in a heat wave, with nothing on the head | 2 to 4 days | A hat; tending
Smoke cough | 4 hours in a closed room of 60 cells or fewer with a wood fire burning | 1 to 2 days | Clean air, a bigger room
Toothache | Sweets and age (more from 40, more again from 60) | Weeks, or a day or two after tending | One good treatment
Stiff neck | A night on the ground, a bedroll or a hard bed | 1 to 2 days | A proper bed
Sprained ankle | 2 hours on the move over marsh, mud, sand, shallow water or deep snow | 5 to 10 days | Bed rest at first, strapping
Eye strain | 4 hours of research or bench work in the dark | A night's sleep | A light at the bench
Rimrot cough (invented) | Nights in a damp room: dirty and under rock, open to the rain, or grimy in a swamp or jungle | 5 to 8 days | A clean, dry, roofed bedroom
Ash lung (invented) | An hour of firefighting, or 4 hours under volcanic ash | 3 to 6 days | Clean air, rest
Splinter | 4 hours of felling or harvesting trees | 4 to 7 days, or one tending | One tending; gloves
Plant rash | 5 hours growing or cutting plants outdoors above 10 °C | 4 to 7 days | Washing, gloves; tending, industrial best
Insect bites | 3 hours outdoors in a swamp or jungle at 18 °C or more | 2 to 3 days | Nets and long sleeves; tending
Heat rash | 6 hours at 32 °C or more (27 °C in a swamp or jungle), awake or asleep | 1 to 2 days | Cooler rooms, loose clothes
Frostnip | 3 hours outdoors below -10 °C | About a day | A hood, a scarf and mittens; bed rest
Nosebleed | 2 hours outdoors below -10 °C | 2 to 4 hours | A scarf over the face
Athlete's foot | 3 hours on the move through water, marsh or mud | 5 to 8 days | Dry feet; tending, industrial best
Motion sickness | 3 hours with a caravan on the move (more in children, less in the old) | Under a day | Tending; it ends when the caravan does

Lice | Nights in a dirty room of 4 or more beds, or unwashed in a shared room; they pass to roommates in dirty rooms | 10 to 17 days, a day or two with tending | Tending and a clean room; while someone has lice, typhus is 3 times as likely

Insomnia | 8 hours of worry in a day (mood under 30%, or strain of 30 or more), or 3 hours awake between midnight and five (never night owls) | About a week | A regular bedtime and fewer late nights; tending
Migraine | 6 hours hungry or 6 hours of worry in a day (rarely in children) | About a day, half that in bed | A dark room and rest; tending, industrial best
Cold sore | 8 hours of worry or 4 hours in the midday heat; 1 in 10 colds leave one | 4 to 7 days | Tending, industrial best (an antiviral)
Heartburn | A fine or lavish meal: 4% each, half again from 40 and double from 60 | 6 to 10 hours | Smaller helpings
Hiccups | An alcoholic drink (5%) or a rich meal (1%) | 1 to 2 hours | Nothing; they stop

li.after: Once a day holds enough hours of the cause, the ailment gets one small chance that day, from under 1% for a cold sore from worry and 1.5% for a sprained ankle to 12% for ash lung after a fire; heartburn and hiccups are rolled with each meal or drink instead. Someone who works hard at one thing every day gets an ailment about once a month, the same one again only after 6 days or more for most (3 to 5 for nosebleeds, frostnip and insect bites, a day or two for hiccups and heartburn), and never more than two at once.

li.heading: Serious illnesses

table.li: Illness | Based on | How it comes | Untreated | With care

Tetanus | Lockjaw, a toxin from soil bacteria | A bite, scratch, stab, cut or gunshot wound left untended for 8 hours: 5% per wound, 40% of that in industrial colonies and 20% in spacer ones, which vaccinate. It shows 3 to 7 days later | Kills in about 7 days | 13 to 19 days of stiffness

Pneumonia | Bacterial pneumonia | A cold, chest cold or flu in someone 60 or older, a small child, or someone frail, starving or chilled: 3% a day (half a percent for anyone else) | Kills in 4 to 5 days | 5 to 8 days, then weakness and a cough

Tuberculosis | Tuberculosis (consumption) | Rarely, one colonist falls ill; it spreads to people asleep in the same room and shows 10 to 20 days later | Wastes away over about 49 days | 36 to 56 days of daily treatment; stopping early lets it come back

Typhus | Epidemic typhus, carried by lice | Nights in a dirty room of 4 or more beds, or unwashed in a shared room: 1.5% a night, 4.5% for someone who has lice; lice spread it in dirty rooms. It shows 4 to 8 days later | Kills in about 6 days | 4 to 5 days with industrial medicine, 8 to 10 with herbal
Meningitis | Bacterial meningitis | Rarely, out of nowhere | Kills in about 2 days | 3 to 5 days, if a skilled doctor tends it at once
Scurvy | Lack of vitamin C | 20 days without fruit or vegetables, raw or in meals: 25% a day | Turns fatal after about 50 more days | Clears within about 10 days of fresh food
Glassblood | Invented: spores in ancient dust | 2 hours of work on ancient walls, caskets or junk: 2.5% a day. It shows a day or two later | Kills in about 6 days | 10 to 12 days

Cholera | Cholera | Rarely, out of nowhere while it's 18 °C or warmer outside; it spreads to people asleep in the same dirty room. It shows half a day to 2 days later | Kills in 2 to 3 days | 3 to 5 days: keeping the patient drinking (steady tending) matters more than the medicine

Appendicitis | Appendicitis | Rarely, out of nowhere; never twice in one person | Kills in about 3 days | Surgery cures it at once ("remove appendix": two medicine, Medicine 4); without it, 4 to 7 days of steady tending, a close thing with herbs alone

Rabies | Rabies | A bite from a warm-blooded animal: 3% on a day bitten, half that if every bite was dressed within 4 hours | Symptoms after about 10 days, then fatal within 3 | Treatment every day before the symptoms show: about 4 to 7 days with industrial medicine, about 3 weeks with herbal. Once they show, nothing helps

Measles | Measles | Rarely, to children only; it spreads to children asleep in the same room. It shows 5 to 8 days later, and a child who has had it never gets it again | Can't kill; about 10 days | Rest and tending ease it
Kidney stone | Kidney stones | Rarely, to adults, twice as often while it's 25 °C or warmer outside | Can't kill; passes in 5 to 7 days | Tending eases the pain and speeds it, industrial best

Shingles | Shingles: the chickenpox virus waking again | Rarely, to people of 50 or older | Can't kill; 2 to 3 weeks, and 3 in 10 have nerve pain for a week or two after | Tending, industrial best (an antiviral)
Hive fever | Invented: insectoid saliva | An insectoid's bite or sting: 4% on a day stung. It shows within a day | Kills in about 5 days | 7 to 10 days

li.after: Herbal medicine in a good doctor's hands (70% tend quality, tending kept up) brings a patient through every one of the fatal ones, though appendicitis comes close and rabies takes weeks. With poorer care, tetanus and meningitis are often fatal without modern medicine, and pneumonia, cholera and appendicitis without any medicine, much as they were in history. A new serious illness never starts within 30 days of the last; tuberculosis, typhus and cholera can spread to at most 3 people, measles to 4 children.

li.heading: Medicine, rest and recovery
li.text:
Tending works as it does for any illness: the doctor's skill and the medicine set the quality, and the illness eases while the treatment lasts, 8 hours for meningitis up to 3 days for a strapped ankle. On top of that, the kind of medicine counts the way it would against the real illness. For colds, coughs and strains it barely matters. For the illnesses real doctors treat with antibiotics, an antitoxin or a vaccine it matters a great deal: industrial medicine works 1.3 to 1.4 times as well as usual against tetanus, pneumonia, typhus, meningitis, appendicitis, rabies and hive fever, herbal medicine (or none) only 0.6 to 0.8 times (0.85 against rabies), and against tuberculosis herbs do half as much. Cholera is the exception: what saves a patient is fluids, so herbs do nearly as well (0.9 against 1.2). Rabies only responds to treatment before its symptoms show; after that, nothing slows it. A patient's tooltip says which medicine was used last and how well it works on that illness.
Bed rest helps the body build immunity, as with any disease, and also speeds a strained back, a sprained ankle and the weakness after an illness. Many illnesses end with an after-effect: a lingering cough for a week or so after a cold, a chest cold, pneumonia or tuberculosis, now and then a cold sore after a cold, nerve pain for a week or two after shingles, and some days of weakness (convalescing, with slower work) after a serious illness or the operation for appendicitis. Nothing is permanent.

li.heading: Settings
li.text: On the People page: Everyday ailments (on by default), Serious illnesses under it (on by default, so the fatal ones can be turned off alone), and how often, from 25% to 200%, which scales every chance and the clock for everything on this page. Turned off, nothing new starts, and whatever is already running finishes its course. Rimfolk's deeper game hooks watch the colony's meals; with them off, scurvy, heartburn and hiccups never start and toothache only comes with age.

li.heading: With Rimfolk
li.text: The moods of everyday ailments feed the heart's frustration; those of serious illnesses feed fear, which builds a little strain, and pain builds strain as it always does. It works the other way too: a strained or unhappy colonist is likelier to lie awake, get migraines and cold sores. A doctor who takes on a serious case feels the weight of it and is more likely to ask the council for a stocked infirmary if medicine is short; pulling a patient through lifts both of them. Patients and doctors write about it in their journals, dreamfever and serious illnesses bring dreams of their own, and while a sickness spreads through the region (a world event), ailments go round two-thirds again as often.
